title: staleness-is-about-this-process-not-about-disk
intention: The ground loop must decide 'is this import failure the device's fault or my own age?' from evidence that is ABOUT THIS PROCESS. Today it decides from the mtime embedded in the .pyc, which is a disk-to-disk comparison any interpreter can refresh — so a second process importing the module repairs the evidence without repairing the loop, and the loop benches an innocent device. Fix both faces: the loud one (a misattributed bench) and the quiet one (a probe that loads fine and evaluates boot-time dependency code).
why: Measured tonight, and it is a fix that did not hold. ground-loop-is-older-than-the-code-it-judges was cleared 2026-08-18T00:51Z by restarting the loop; 2h53m later the same condition benched the survey device at 03:44:07Z for an ImportError the disk does not have. The guard stayed silent because my own proof run had rewritten inspector.py's .pyc header 67s after the edit, so module_drift read the module CURRENT while the loop still held the pre-edit object. The consequence is not cosmetic: a benched device's watches never fire, and the probe armed by tonight's PROVED voyage is dark right now.
traces_to: Law 3 (nothing is known until measured — a bench is a verdict about whose fault it is, and it is being issued from evidence that cannot answer the question) and Law 10 (the distinction this law is made of: 'we have not built the measurement yet' is ordinary; the measurement WAS built and reads the wrong thing, which is worse, because it looks like it answered).

falsifier.proves_red: FALSIFIER: after this lands, no device is benched for an import failure that a FRESH interpreter does not reproduce. Directly instrumented, and over the live store rather than a fixture — for every standing ground-loop-device-* trouble, re-run the named folder's import in a subprocess; a success is a misattribution and the falsifier has fired. Today that instrument reads 1: ground-loop-device-survey, raised 2026-08-18T03:44:07Z, whose folder imports clean in a fresh process (1 probe, 0 failures, measured before this cast). SECOND FALSIFIER, for the quiet half: a probe whose dependency was edited after the loop booted evaluates the edited code, not the boot-time code. HORIZON: 30 days, and the horizon is short on purpose — this is the SECOND time this condition has been fixed. The first fix (ticket the-loop-names-its-own-staleness-instead-of-benching-a-device) shipped staleness.py, was cleared 2026-08-18T00:51Z by killing pid 3933751 and relaunching, and was defeated 2h53m later by an ordinary proof run in the same tree.
